uncited: This family encompasses methods that utilize deep neural networks to solve the inverse problem of tomographic reconstruction, mapping measured projection data (sinograms) directly or iteratively to a 3D volume estimate.

Unlike classical analytical methods (e.g., Filtered Back-Projection) or iterative algebraic techniques, these methods leverage the expressive power of neural architectures to regularize the ill-posed nature of the inverse Radon transform, particularly in sparse-view or noisy regimes.

They are distinguished from [Neural Radiance Fields and Implicit Neural Representations](13341-neural-radiance-fields-and-implicit-neural-representations.md) by their explicit focus on tomographic geometry (Radon transforms) and often their ability to produce explicit voxel-based or parametric density volumes suitable for quantitative analysis, rather than just view-dependent rendering.
**Backward Projection (Adjoint):** Distributing the error from the 2D detector plane back into the 3D volume.

*   **Pitfall:** MRI intensities do not correspond directly to physical quantities such as density or acoustic impedance; they reflect a complex combination of tissue-specific properties (water content, fat concentration, relaxation times) modulated by the acquisition sequence.
The application of deep learning to tomographic reconstruction has evolved from post-processing denoising to end-to-end inverse solvers.
Early works focused on using CNNs to denoise Filtered Back-Projection (FBP) outputs.
